title: Rosalind and the Passage
premise: Lena Okafor, a mountain guide blacklisted from two countries after a client's death she didn't cause, survives by leading undocumented crossings through the Verren Range. A dying prospector named Aldous Vane trades her his map to an unregistered silver lode in exchange for her promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter, Mireille, before the concession permits expire and the claim reverts to the mining consortium that ruined him. Pursued by the consortium's enforcer and a magistrate who wants Lena's silence bought, she and her estranged climbing partner Tomas race the snows across the range, discovering the lode sits on land the consortium illegally poisoned. At the pass, Lena chooses justice over the claim itself: she gives the map to the displaced valley communities, exposes the consortium's permits as fraudulent, and clears her own name at the cost of the fortune and, briefly, Tomas. The book ends with Lena guiding one last legal crossing, finally allowed to stop.
about_author: Rosalind Kavanagh is a former alpine rescue volunteer who spent a decade in remote mountain towns before turning to fiction full-time. Her novels are known for brutal landscapes, morally tangled characters, and endings that cost their heroes something real.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. She leads a family of undocumented migrants over a low col, paid in cash and silence, and learns at the trailhead that her name has been posted in a third border town. The emotional beat is exhaustion sharpened into defiance: stopping is no longer an option, and she knows it.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Last Inn
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. In a half-empty mountain inn she meets Aldous Vane, a coughing prospector who recognizes her from her blacklisted days. He buys her dinner and asks dangerous questions about the high passes. The beat is wary curiosity; Lena smells trouble but also the first real money in months.

chapters.title: The Map and the Promise
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane, dying, shows her a hand-drawn map to an unregistered silver lode and offers it for one promise: deliver it to his daughter Mireille in the valley town of Corven before the concession permits expire in six weeks. The beat is temptation curdling into obligation as Lena realizes what she's being asked to carry.

chapters.title: What Tomas Knows
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Lena's former climbing partner, now a licensed guide on the legal side of the range, learns she's back and confronts her in a supply depot. Old wounds surface: the client who died on their last shared expedition. The beat is anger masking grief, and a grudging offer to help she refuses.

chapters.title: Vane Dies at Dawn
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Vane dies before they can set out together, leaving Lena with the map, his journal, and a consortium enforcer named Brakke asking questions at the inn. The beat is cold fear; the map is now evidence, a target, and a debt all at once.

chapters.title: Corven
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV. In Corven, Vane's estranged daughter works at a clinic serving communities sickened by mine runoff, despising the father who abandoned her. She doesn't know he's dead. The beat is bitter resentment that the narrative will slowly complicate.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Magistrate Ilse Renn captures Lena at a checkpoint and offers to expunge her record if she surrenders the map and testifies that Vane sold it to her willingly. The beat is the first real taste of justice-as-bargain, and Lena's refusal, which she already regrets.

chapters.title: Over the Wall by Night
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena escapes Renn's custody and crosses into the high range illegally, forcing her onto routes only she knows. The beat is exhilaration and terror in equal measure; the mountain is the one place she's never been a criminal.

chapters.title: Tomas Follows
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas abandons a paying client season to follow Lena's trail, telling himself it's about the truth of the old accident, not her. He intercepts her at a bivouac. The beat is a fragile, prickly alliance sealed by a storm rolling in early.

chapters.title: The Poisoned Valley
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Descending for supplies, they find a valley village where the water runs grey and children are ill — downstream of consortium operations. The map's lode sits directly above. The beat is moral vertigo: the claim Vane died for is on poisoned ground.

chapters.title: Brakke on the Trail
chapters.summary: Brakke's POV. The enforcer closes in, using Renn's authority as cover, and burns a supply cache to starve Lena and Tomas off the mountain. The beat is menace; Brakke is revealed as a man who genuinely believes order is worth any price.

chapters.title: Mireille's Ledger
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV. Mireille, investigating her father's name, finds his old letters and evidence that the consortium's permits were obtained fraudulently — and that he spent years trying to prove it alone. The beat is grief arriving ahead of forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Glacier Crossing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena and Tomas attempt the glacier traverse as the snows close in early. A crevasse fall nearly kills Tomas, and Lena saves him in a reversal of the accident that broke them. The beat is terror transmuted into something like trust.

chapters.title: What Happened on the Kessel Face
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Shelterbound by the storm, Tomas finally tells his side of the fatal expedition: the client ignored orders, and Lena took the blame to protect the client's widow. The beat is devastating relief — the lie that exiled Lena was a kindness neither could speak.

chapters.title: Renn's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Renn, now compromised by Brakke's methods, finds them at a waystation and offers a darker deal: the map for Lena's freedom and Tomas's immunity. Lena realizes Renn is no longer the enemy she should fear. The beat is a bargain refused on new, clearer terms.

chapters.title: The Descent to Corven
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Racing the first real snowfall, they descend the dangerous east face with Brakke's party tracking them. A rockfall kills one of Brakke's hired men and forces a stalemate. The beat is grim arithmetic — everyone is now spending lives to reach the same valley.

chapters.title: The Daughter's Door
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena reaches Corven and faces Mireille, who wants nothing from the father who left. Lena gives her the map and the journal and tells her how he died keeping his promise. The beat is grief finally landing where it belongs.

chapters.title: Permit Day
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV. On the day the permits expire, Mireille walks into the concession hearing with the journal, the map, and testimony from the poisoned valley. Renn, cornered, sides against Brakke. The beat is quiet, procedural courage — justice arriving not with violence but with paperwork and nerve.

chapters.title: Brakke's Last Climb
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Brakke attempts to seize the original map from Lena at the trailhead; a violent struggle on the scree ends with Brakke clinging to a slope and Lena choosing to save him. The beat is the thesis made flesh: she refuses to become what she's fighting.

chapters.title: The Claim
chapters.summary: Mireille's POV. The permits are voided and the land's remediation ordered; the lode's value goes to the valley communities as restitution, not fortune. Mireille buries her father's journal at the lode itself. The beat is the price of survival paid forward instead of collected.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. With Renn's testimony and the consortium's collapse, Lena's blacklist is overturned — the truth of the Kessel Face finally on record. Tomas, offered a partnership in the low valleys, chooses it, and they part as friends. The beat is bittersweet: love against duty resolves into duty honored, love released.

chapters.title: One Last Crossing
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Months later, Lena leads her first fully legal crossing, migrants with real papers, Mireille waving from the Corven clinic. On the col, she stops for the first time in years and looks back at the range. The beat is stillness earned: the map is spent, the promise kept, and moving is finally a choice.
